speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth with respect to the Report of the Auditor-General for FY 2020/2021 (a) why did the People's Association (PA) not adopt the Government's instruction to adopt full price fluctuation in construction contracts; (b) how long has the PA practised this incorrect methodology; and (c) what is the total value of the contracts that invoked this incorrect methodology over the last seven years.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth with respect to the Report of the Auditor-General for FY2020/2021 (a) whether PA will undertake an extensive review, investigation or audit to ascertain the true extent of lapses in approvals found in more than 50% of PA's contract variations on a test-check basis; and (b) what is the facility referred to and who is the managing agent identified in paragraph 56 of the Report where out of 36 supporting documents for the project, 34 were suspected to have been falsified amongst other irregularities.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The findings by AGO relate to these two projects.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I will address the questions from several Members of the House relating to three key findings by AGO.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But before I go into the specific findings, let me provide some context and background to these projects.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It does this through a wide range of programmes that cater to residents of different profiles and interests.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Community facilities play an important part in terms of providing the infrastructure that supports us in bringing people together.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: During times of crisis, in particular, these community nodes become critical points of support for our residents.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For instance, in our fight against COVID-19, PA transformed its community clubs (CCs) and residents' committee (RC) centres into distribution networks.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We were able to quickly give our residents much-needed masks, sanitisers, TraceTogether tokens, Antigen Rapid Test (ART) test kits and so on.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Almost overnight, many CCs were also turned into Vaccination Centres, to support our nation-wide vaccination efforts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Today, PA manages a total of 788 community facilities which vary in size and offerings.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These range from the CCs and RC centres to specialist CCs such as PAssion WaVe and imPAct @ Hong Lim Green.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: At any given point in time, about 50 of its facilities would be undergoing development or redevelopments.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These include construction of new facilities, upgrading works, cyclical maintenance or minor building works.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In 2010, the Government embarked on plans to build integrated community hubs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The intention was to bring together Government services with community programming and other related businesses under one roof, to better and more conveniently serve residents.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For each of our integrated community hubs, PA took on the responsibility as the lead agency to undertake its development, working closely with various Government agencies, industry stakeholders and also, professionals.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In each of these two cases, external consultants such as quantity surveyors, architects, engineers, project managers and managing agents (MA) were engaged, to help advise on and manage the construction phase of the development and subsequently, upon its completion, the management and maintenance of the facility.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These two developments added to the stable of PA's facilities, which were useful to meet growing and varied community demands.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: OTH is Singapore's largest integrated community and lifestyle hub.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It offers more than 30 sporting, lifestyle, community, performing arts facilities and also, it is Singapore's first Integrated Public Service Centre.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Residents have one-stop access to more than 450 Government services by 18 Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: HBB is Singapore's second community hub, located at Bedok Town Centre.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Like OTH, HBB houses multiple agencies and facilities, including a polyclinic, senior care centre, ActiveSG sport centre, public library as well as food and beverage (F&B) and other retail outlets.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Pritam Singh asked about the adoption of full price fluctuation in relation to OTH's main construction contracts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For all public construction developments with a contract value of more than $5 million, the Government requires agencies to adopt full price fluctuation adjustment for key construction materials, specifically, concrete and steel reinforcement.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is to encourage companies, the bidders, to put in a more realistic bid for public sector projects.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: AGO observed that the full price fluctuation was not adopted in the case of OTH's main construction contract.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When PA did its investigations, it found that this had been discussed and proposed by PA's appointed team of external consultants and was then accepted by PA.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: However, this was a mistake as PA should have adopted full price fluctuation instead, in accordance with the Government’s instruction.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Following this finding, PA undertook a review of the 31 relevant public construction developments over the last seven years.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It found that, in this period, two other construction projects had also erroneously adopted a 70% price fluctuation adjustment, instead of a full price fluctuation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On these two construction projects, the preliminary calculation is that if a full price fluctuation had been adopted instead, this would have resulted in a price adjustment differential of about $60,000 in favour of PA.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: PA has since ensured that the provision in all such similar standard construction contracts is clear and is fixed, to ensure greater clarity and compliance on how price fluctuation adjustments should be made, as per the requirement for all Government projects.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It has also been reiterated to relevant officers who oversee such projects to ensure compliance.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Next, Sir, let me address AGO's findings on the management and oversight of contract variations.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This applies for the main construction contracts during the development phase of both OTH and HBB.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The lapses relate to improper approval processes for variation works that had been conducted.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The AGO found that there was a lack of evidence of approvals and in some cases, approvals which were given after the works had commenced or were already completed.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And in some other cases, approvals for the increase in variation costs were not documented.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: AGO opined that these lapses indicated weaknesses in the monitoring of contract variations and inadequate oversight of the consultants by PA.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Subsequent to AGO's findings, PA undertook a thorough check on all 252 cases flagged by AGO.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The check showed that whilst there were inadequate or missing documentations in respect of those variation works identified by AGO, these variation works were in fact requested for and approved.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: PA was able to independently verify, including through contemporaneous materials, that the variation works were carried out following discussions and decisions taken at project site meetings between PA and its consultants, and following the issuance of work orders.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: However, the project staff and consultants at that time, did not maintain proper documentation of these decisions, resulting in AGO’s observations.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is a lapse which has to be addressed.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In addition, PA is now undertaking a full review of the remaining contract variations, beyond those sampled by AGO, for the main construction contracts for these two developments.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Whilst these were not part of AGO’s test check requirements, PA is doing so, to ensure that the contract variations were carried out with the appropriate approvals and proper documentation, and if not, then to take the appropriate remedial actions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To further improve the future management of contract variations, PA has since also implemented the following: one, required the reporting and monitoring of contract variations in project progress meetings as a standard form; two, published a manual on contract variation process and procedures to further guide PA staff and its external consultants in the management of contract variations; and three, established an e-filing system for documenting variation approvals to enhance oversight and tracking.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Pritam Singh, Ms Foo Mee Har and Mr Sitoh Yih Pin have raised questions with regard to this observation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: AGO's findings under this heading relate to transactions carried out in conjunction with minor building works at the facility, undertaken by external contractors during the maintenance phase of OTH.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In respect to these works, PA had engaged an external managing agent to support the onsite facilities management team and also, supervise the works by the contractors.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When PA was notified by AGO on the irregularities observed, an internal investigation panel was immediately convened to look into these transactions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This panel was led by senior officers from PA and the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth to conduct a thorough review of the related processes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: PA took a very serious view of these irregularities.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In addition, the staff who were directly involved have also been suspended pending the outcome of these investigations.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: PA is presently reviewing each of these transactions to ascertain if any losses have been occasioned by these irregularities and if so, to take the appropriate recovery action.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the meantime, to ensure that the operations and maintenance of facilities at OTH carries on without disruption, PA has set up a task force to review and take steps to strengthen existing processes in procurement, contract and facility management, all of which, carry on at OTH.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Second, to also improve staffing resources, including the appropriate oversight of contractors and managing agents.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin has asked if PA will conduct a thorough investigation into all payments made in relation to OTH's facility maintenance contracts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The internal audit team has since undertaken a sample review of all the other facility maintenance contracts entered into by OTH and did not find any irregularities similar in nature as those flagged by AGO.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Sitoh also asked whether PA's internal audit team had picked up any of these lapses raised by AGO.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The internal audit team identifies key compliance risk areas and conducts sample checks to detect lapses or non-compliance.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In addition to compliance and operational audits, PA also engages an external auditor to conduct annual audits on its financial information.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The integrated community hubs that I have mentioned, are audited regularly on a cyclical basis.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: PA last audited OTH and HBB in 2018 and 2019 respectively.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: At that time, these developments had just started their operations and the audits then were focused on procurement, revenue and tenancy management.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: PA's internal audit did not uncover any significant discrepancies, nor did AGO highlight any issues with respect to these three areas.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In February 2020, PA's internal audit had included in their FY2021 workplan to conduct checks on OTH and HBB.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The checks were to be focused on the facilities' development and maintenance relating to progress claims, documentation and term contracts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These plans were, however, put on hold when AGO began its audit of OTH and HBB in July 2020.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The planned areas of audit for OTH in FY2021 were eventually covered under AGO's audit that was conducted in FY2020.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ms Foo, in particular, asked about the control measures.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The external consultant will have a broad mandate to review.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They will make practical recommendations to rectify control weakness or lapses noted as well as identify areas of improvement in terms of efficiency, economy and effectiveness.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: PA will take in the recommendations, improve processes where needed and implement better oversight.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And PA takes the findings of AGO very seriously.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is underscored by how immediate steps were taken to review the observations, going beyond AGO's findings and subsequently, the remedial steps that I outlined earlier.
